messages.author: 5196f936ff792c35
messages.subject: Dropping unused levels in plot call
parts:
Hi All, 

This is a minor nuisance, but I'm subsetting my data in the ggplot() call and I want it to drop the unused levels of Variety while subsetting by melon type. When I use drop=T it just seems to ignore it since the MD melons end up in the legend anyway. 

Is there a simple nuance to this that I'm missing? 

Brandon

I'm sorry it's not "minimal," but here is everything. The MD#### data aren't plotted and shouldn't be in the legend, but are. :/

require(ggplot2)
melon.pack2.nd.avg<-structure(list(Variety = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 
3L, 3L, 4L, 4L, 4L, 5L, 5L, 5L, 6L, 6L, 6L, 7L, 7L, 7L, 8L, 8L, 
8L, 9L, 9L, 9L, 10L, 10L, 10L, 11L, 11L, 11L, 12L, 12L, 12L), .Label = c("ALONSO", 
"CEZANNE", "GANDALF", "ZICO", "ANASTA", "ARAPAHO", "MATCH", "NEO", 
"GLOBSTAR", "MAGENTA", "MD2088", "MD2537"), class = "factor"), 
    Shelf.Life = structure(c(3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 3L, 
    3L, 3L, 3L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 
    1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("LSL", 
    "MSL", "SSL"), class = "factor"), Melon.type = structure(c(1L, 
    1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 
    1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 
    2L, 2L, 2L, 2L), .Label = c("Charentais", "Galia"), class = "factor"), 
    Days2 = structure(c(1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 
    3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 
    3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L, 2L, 3L), .Label = c("Harvest", 
    "Ripe", "Overripe"), class = "factor"), mean.avg = c(7.02666666666667, 
    2.57666666666667, 3.70333333333333, 2.69, 2.24666666666667, 
    7.66, 4.58666666666667, 2.44666666666667, 17.4866666666667,

    16.3966666666667, 16.3133333333333, 10.225, 11.0633333333333, 
    4.43333333333333, 6.12333333333333), dataset.se = c(0.915429468124722, 
    0.736168760845259, 1.42390698822329, 0.190087699058443, 0.763966258708096, 
    1.51741007421637, 0.496800876721359, 0.212629045784227, 2.51333333333333, 
    0.9477048298096, 0.429974159430282, 2.80666666666667, 0.586524604011725, 
    0.208513255640445, 0.437200691267117, 0.36671211839504, 0.732416093032733,

    3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3, 3)), .Names = c("Variety", 
"Shelf.Life", "Melon.type", "Days2", "mean.avg", "dataset.se", 
"count"), row.names = c(NA, 35L), class = "data.frame")

ggplot(data=melon.pack2.nd.avg[melon.pack2.nd.avg$Melon.type == "Charentais", ], aes(Days2, mean.avg, group=Variety)) +

geom_line(aes(color=Variety))+

geom_point(aes(color=Variety))+

scale_y_continuous('FIRMNESS')+

scale_x_discrete('Stage of Ripeness')+

theme_bw()+

opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(colour = "black", vjust=1)

, axis.text.y = theme_text(colour="black", hjust=1)

, legend.key = theme_blank())+

geom_errorbar(aes(ymax=mean.avg+dataset.se, ymin=mean.avg-dataset.se), width=0.1, size=0.5, alpha=0.35)


##Attempting to drop the unused levels...

ggplot(data=melon.pack2.nd.avg[melon.pack2.nd.avg$Melon.type == "Charentais", ,drop=T], aes(Days2, mean.avg, group=Variety)) +

geom_line(aes(color=Variety))+

geom_point(aes(color=Variety))+

scale_y_continuous('FIRMNESS')+

scale_x_discrete('Stage of Ripeness')+

theme_bw()+

opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(colour = "black", vjust=1)

, axis.text.y = theme_text(colour="black", hjust=1)

, legend.key = theme_blank())+

geom_errorbar(aes(ymax=mean.avg+dataset.se, ymin=mean.avg-dataset.se), width=0.1, size=0.5, alpha=0.35)

parts: hi

currently, the easiest way is probably to drop the unused factor level
before passing to ggplot:

d<-subset(melon.pack2.nd.avg, Melon.type == "Charentais")
d$Variety<-factor(d$Variety)
ggplot(data=d, ...

and in R 2.12.0, which will appear in this month, has a new function
droplevels()
then you can do by:

ggplot(data=droplevels(subset(melon.pack2.nd.avg, Melon.type ==
"Charentais")), ...

messages.subject: Re: Dropping unused levels in plot call
parts:
Hadley, 

I think I saw that you said something similar on a Nabble or LearnR blog or something. The only issue is that I have ordered my Varieties in a very particularly way so that each type is a row (can you order a character list?).  As far as I know, this means that Variety has to be a factor, which means that when I subset it (and keep the correct order of things) that I'm subsetting a factor and the extra labels are retained.  

Am I just being lazy? I swear I'm not trying to be. I just want something that will let me show some beautiful graphs to my boss so he's happy, with as little fuss as possible. 

Speaking of which... is this it? 

droplevels <- function(x, ...) UseMethod("droplevels")

droplevels.factor <- function(x, ...) factor(x)

droplevels.data.frame <- function(x, except = NULL, ...)

  {      

    ix <- sapply(x, is.factor)

    if (!is.null(except)) ix[except] <- FALSE

    x[ix] <- lapply(x[ix], factor)

    x

  }


I think it works... 


Brandon

droplevels.factor <- function(x, ...) factor(x)

droplevels.data.frame <- function(x, except = NULL, ...)

  {      

    ix <- sapply(x, is.factor)

    if (!is.null(except)) ix[except] <- FALSE

    x[ix] <- lapply(x[ix], factor)

    x

  }

Ben and all,

I just ran the code I pulled from the subset.r file in the nightly
build and it worked great with the usage that Takahashi suggested. R
2.12.0 is supposed to be released on the 15th or so.

droplevels <- function(x, ...) UseMethod("droplevels")
droplevels.factor <- function(x, ...) factor(x)
droplevels.data.frame <- function(x, except = NULL, ...)
{
ix <- sapply(x, is.factor)
if (!is.null(except)) ix[except] <- FALSE
x[ix] <- lapply(x[ix], factor)
x
}
